chunks: My father - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Ma’bad, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'How many people does a camel suffice for?' He replied, 'For one person.' I asked, 'And what about a cow?' He replied, 'It suffices for five, if they eat together at one table.' I asked, 'Why does the camel not suffice for anyone but one, while the cow suffices for five?' He replied, 'Because the camel did not contain the reason (illah) that was present in the cow. Indeed, those who commanded the people of Moses (peace be upon him) to worship the calf were five individuals. They were a family who ate together at one table: Azinooneh, his brother Mabzooneh, his brother's son, his daughter, and his wife. They were the ones who commanded the worship of the calf, and they were the same ones who slaughtered the cow which God, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded to be slaughtered.'

key_terms.الْبَدَنَةُ: A mature camel used for sacrifice
key_terms.الْعِلَّةُ: The legal reason or cause behind a ruling

ai.seo_question: Why does a cow suffice for five people in sacrifice while a camel only suffices for one?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the jurisprudential cause (illah) for the difference in sacrificial validity between a camel and a cow by linking it to the historical precedent of the five family members of the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf. He explains that since these five individuals, who were related and shared a single table, were responsible for both the calf incident and the subsequent slaughter of the cow commanded in Surah Al-Baqarah, the cow is deemed sufficient for five people, whereas the camel, lacking this specific historical connection, is limited to one. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly method of deriving legal rulings from historical narratives (asbab al-wurud) and the wisdom behind divine commands.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 32-22 My father - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Ma’bad that Al-Husayn ibn Khalid asked Abil Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.),

“For how many people is the offering of a camel (for sacrifice on the ‘Eid ul-Adha) enough of an offering?” Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) replied, “One.” Then he asked, “What about offering a cow?” Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) replied, “For five individuals it is enough, if they spend and eat together.” Then he asked, “Why does offering one cow suffice for five people while offering a camel does not?” Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) replied, “It is because of the reason there lies behind a camel which does not lie behind a cow. The people of the Children of Israel who invited the people to worship the calf were five. They were all from the same home and they all ate together. They were Azinooneh, his brother Mabzooneh, his brother’s son, his daughter and his wife. They were the ones who invited the people to worship the calf. They were the same ones who killed the cow which God had ordered to be offered for sacrifice.”
